profiles.name: Elizabeth Minnie Huff
profiles.query: "Elizabeth Minnie Huff" suffrage Huff Johnson portrait photograph archive
profiles.identity_context:
Elizabeth Minnie Huff was a member of the National Woman's Party and one of the "Silent Sentinels" imprisoned during the 1917-1919 campaign to picket the Wilson White House for woman suffrage. The exact day of her death is unresolved. (January 28, 1891 - 1989; later Elizabeth Minnie Huff Johnson and sometimes recorded as Elisabeth Minnie Johnson)

She was arrested on January 13, 1919 and released on bail, then rearrested that evening and held overnight. On January 14 she was sentenced to five days in the District Jail. No discharge record has been found; the sentence would nominally have run to January 19, which is a calculation rather than a record.

On the name: Doris Stevens's appendix lists her as "Elizabeth Hoff", and this record was previously filed under that spelling. Inez Haynes Irwin's contemporary history of the National Woman's Party names Elizabeth Huff among those arrested on January 13, and the biographical record confirms Huff. "Hoff" appears to be a variant or slip in Stevens.
profiles.finding: Alexander Street biography independently establishes Huff/Elisabeth Minnie Johnson identity and references Find a Grave100165950; embedded image1009755067-I001 remains a portrait lead for inspection.
